title.zh: 卷三八 補列傳第三十 辛術 元文遙 趙彥深
title.en: Volume 38 Biographies 30: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen
title.raw: 卷三八 補列傳第三十 辛術 元文遙 趙彥深 Volume 38 Biographies 30: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen

sentences.zh: 辛術 元文遙 趙彥深

translations.literal: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen

sentences.zh: 辛術，字懷哲，少明敏，有識度。

translations.literal: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, from youth was bright and keen, with judgment and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, was clever and perceptive from boyhood, with a steady sense of what mattered.

sentences.zh: 解褐司空胄曹參軍，與僕射高隆之共典營構鄴都宮室，術有思理，百工克濟。

translations.literal: Upon first office he was Staff Member in the Registrar's Office of the Directorate of Works; together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw the construction of Ye's palaces—Shu had thoughtful designs, and all the crafts were brought to completion.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was staff member in the registrar's office of the directorate of works; with vice director Gao Longzhi he directed the building of Ye's palaces. Shu planned well, and every trade met its mark.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 出為清河太守，政有能名。

translations.literal: Sent out as Administrator of Qinghe; his governance won a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as administrator of Qinghe, he earned a name for capable rule.

sentences.zh: 追授幷州長史，遭父憂去職。

translations.literal: Retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bing province; he left office on father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was retroactively made chief clerk of Bing province, then left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 清河父老數百人詣闕請立碑頌德。

translations.literal: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the capital to request a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Qinghe elders went to court to ask that a stele be raised in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 文襄嗣事，與尚書左丞宋遊道、中書侍郎李繪等並追詣晉陽，俱為上客。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession, together with Left Vice Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Attendant Li Hui, and others he hurried to Jinyang; all became honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng assumed power, he went with left vice director Song Youdao, secretariat attendant Li Hui, and others to Jinyang and was received as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 武定八年，侯景叛，除東南道行臺尚書，封江夏縣男，與高岳等破侯景，擒蕭明。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled; Shu was appointed Masters of Writing on the Southeastern Circuit Mobile Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangxia county (male), and with Gao Yue and others defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled. Shu was made masters of writing on the southeastern mobile grand secretariat and enfeoffed as marquis of Jiangxia. With Gao Yue and others he broke Hou Jing and took Xiao Ming prisoner.

sentences.zh: 遷東徐州刺史，為淮南經略使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou; made Commissioner for the Pacification of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Eastern Xuzhou and made commissioner for Huainan pacification.

sentences.zh: 齊天保元年，侯景徵江西租稅，術率諸軍渡淮斷之，燒其稻數百萬石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, Hou Jing levied rents and taxes from Jiangxi; Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut it off and burned several million shi of his rice.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's first Tianbao year, Hou Jing levied rents from Jiangxi. Shu led troops across the Huai to block him and burned several million shi of his grain.

sentences.zh: 還鎮下邳，人隨術北渡淮者三千餘家。

translations.literal: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to garrison Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed him north across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 東徐州刺史郭誌殺郡守。

translations.literal: Guo Zhi, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed the commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhi, governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed his commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 文宣聞之，勑術自今所統十餘州地諸有犯法者，刺史先啟聽報，以下先斷後表聞。

translations.literal: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu: from now on in the more than ten provinces under his command, wherever anyone violated the law, the governor should first report and await instruction; subordinates might judge first and memorialize afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu that in the dozen-odd provinces under him, whenever anyone broke the law the governor must first report and wait for word; lower officials might decide first and memorialize later.

sentences.zh: 齊代行臺兼總人事，自術始也。

translations.literal: In Qi, a mobile grand secretariat concurrently overseeing personnel matters began with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi the practice of a mobile grand secretariat also holding personnel authority began with Shu.

sentences.zh: 安州刺史、臨清太守、盱眙蘄城二鎮將犯法，術皆案奏殺之。

translations.literal: The Governor of Anzhou, Administrator of Linqing, and the two garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all violated capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them executed.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Anzhou, the administrator of Linqing, and the garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all committed capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them put to death.

sentences.zh: 睢州刺史及所部郡守俱犯大辟，朝廷以其奴婢百口及資財盡賜術，三辭不見許，術乃送詣所司，不復以聞。

translations.literal: The Governor of Suizhou and all the commandery administrators under him committed capital offenses; the court granted Shu all their hundred-odd slaves and entire assets; he declined three times but was not permitted; Shu then sent them to the relevant office and no longer kept them for himself.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Suizhou and every commandery administrator under him faced capital punishment. The court granted Shu all their slaves—more than a hundred households—and their property. He declined three times and was refused; Shu then turned everything over to the proper office and did not keep it.

sentences.zh: 邢卲聞之，遺術書曰：「昔鐘離意云『孔子忍渴於盜泉』，便以珠璣委地，足下今能如此，可謂異代一時。

translations.literal: Xing Shao heard of it and sent Shu a letter, saying: "In antiquity Zhongli Yi said, 'Confucius bore thirst at Robber Spring,' and thereby cast pearls and jades to the ground; you, sir, can do the same today—one may call it the same moment across different ages.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao heard and wrote Shu: "Long ago Zhongli Yi said that Confucius would endure thirst rather than drink from Robber Spring, and so cast pearls and jade aside; you, sir, can do as much today—truly one moment in another age.

sentences.zh: 」及王僧辯破侯景，術招攜安撫，城鎮相繼款附，前後二十餘州。

translations.literal: " When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited and pacified; cities and garrisons in succession submitted; in all more than twenty provinces.
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu won men over and pacified the land; towns and garrisons submitted one after another—more than twenty provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 於是移鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved his command to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He then shifted his headquarters to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 獲傳國璽送鄴，文宣以璽告於太廟。

translations.literal: He obtained the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang reported the seal at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang presented it at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 此璽卽秦所制，方四寸，上紐交盤龍，其文曰：「受命于天，旣壽永昌。

translations.literal: This seal was that made by Qin, four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons; its inscription read: "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: This was the seal Qin had made: four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons. Its inscription read, "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity.

sentences.zh: 」二漢相傳，又傳魏、晉。

translations.literal: " The Two Han transmitted it; it was also transmitted through Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: " The two Han dynasties passed it down; Wei and Jin passed it down as well.

sentences.zh: 懷帝敗，沒於劉聰。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost among Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 聰敗，沒於石氏。

translations.literal: When Cong was defeated, it was lost among the Shi clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong fell, it passed to the Shi clan.

sentences.zh: 石氏敗，晉穆帝永和中，濮陽太守戴僧施得之，遣督護何融送于建鄴。

translations.literal: When the Shi clan was defeated, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Dai Sengshi, Administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shi fell, in the Yonghe reign of Jin's Emperor Mu, Dai Sengshi, administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 歷宋、齊、梁，梁敗，侯景得之。

translations.literal: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing took it.

sentences.zh: 景敗，侍中趙思賢以璽投景南兗州刺史郭元建，送于術，故術以進焉。

translations.literal: When Jing was defeated, Attendant Zhong Zhao Sixian cast the seal upon Jing's Southern Yanzhou Governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was defeated, attendant-in-ordinary Zhao Sixian gave the seal to Jing's southern Yanzhou governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; thus Shu was able to present it.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為殿中尚書，領太常卿，仍與朝賢議定律令。

translations.literal: Soon summoned as Masters of Writing in the Palace, leading Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and still deliberated on laws and ordinances with court worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned as palace masters of writing and director of the imperial ancestral temple, and still joined court worthies in revising laws and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，食南兗州梁郡幹。

translations.literal: Promoted to Director of Personnel; drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of personnel and drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴以後，大選之職，知名者數四，互有得失，未能盡美。

translations.literal: After the move to Ye, the great selection posts had four well-known holders, each with gain and loss, none attaining perfection.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, four famous men held the great selection office in turn; each had strengths and flaws, and none achieved perfection.

sentences.zh: 文襄帝少年高朗，所弊者疏；

translations.literal: Gao Cheng in his youth was lofty and clear; what harmed him was laxity.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng in his youth was bright and open; his fault was looseness.

sentences.zh: 袁叔德沉密謹厚，所傷者細；

translations.literal: Yuan Shude was deep, close, and cautious; what harmed him was minuteness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shude was grave, careful, and thorough; his fault was excessive detail.

sentences.zh: 楊愔風流辨給，取士失於浮華。

translations.literal: Yang Yin was polished and quick in debate; in selecting men he erred toward flashiness.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin was eloquent and quick; in choosing men he favored show over substance.

sentences.zh: 唯術性尚貞明，取士以才器，循名責實，新舊參舉，管庫必擢，門閥不遺。

translations.literal: Only Shu, by nature upright and clear, chose men by talent and capacity, held names to facts, mixed old and new in nomination, must promote from storehouses, and did not leave out noble houses.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shu, upright by nature, chose by talent and office, matched names to reality, mixed veterans and newcomers, promoted men from the storehouses, and did not overlook great families.

sentences.zh: 考之前後銓衡，在術最為折衷，甚為當時所稱舉。

translations.literal: Reviewing selection before and after, Shu's was most balanced, and was greatly praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing earlier and later rounds of selection, Shu's was the most even-handed, and his age praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 天保末，文宣嘗令術選百員官，參選者二三千人，術題目士子，人無謗讟，其所旌擢，後亦皆致通顯。

translations.literal: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once had Shu select a hundred officials; those who competed numbered two or three thousand; Shu examined the scholars; none slandered; those he honored and promoted later all attained high prominence.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once ordered Shu to choose a hundred officials from two or three thousand candidates. Shu tested the scholars; no one murmured against him, and those he advanced later all rose to high rank.

sentences.zh: 術清儉，寡嗜欲。

translations.literal: Shu was pure and frugal, with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was austere and frugal, with few wants.

sentences.zh: 勤於所職，未嘗暫懈。

translations.literal: Diligent in his duties, never briefly slackening.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in office and never slackened even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 臨軍以威嚴，牧人有惠政。

translations.literal: Facing armies with stern authority; governing the people with beneficent policy.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army he was stern; over the people he ruled with kindness.

sentences.zh: 少愛文史，晚更修學，雖在戎旅，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: In youth he loved literature and history; in later years he studied further; though on campaign, his hand never left the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He loved letters in youth and studied harder in later years; even on campaign he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 及定淮南，凡諸資物一毫無犯，唯大收典籍，多是宋、齊、梁時佳本，鳩集萬餘卷，幷顧、陸之徒名畫、二王已下法書數亦不少，俱不上王府，唯入私門。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, of all goods he touched not a hairsbreadth; he only gathered books in great number—mostly fine editions from Song, Qi, and Liang times—more than ten thousand scrolls collected, together with famous paintings by Gu and Lu and their school, and calligraphies after the Two Wangs in no small number; none went to the imperial storehouse—only into his private gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was settled he took not a thread of booty, but gathered books in force—mostly fine Song, Qi, and Liang editions, more than ten thousand scrolls—along with celebrated paintings by Gu, Lu, and their circle and many works of calligraphy after the Two Wangs. None went to the imperial treasury; all entered his private house.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，頗以饋遺權要，物議以此少之。

translations.literal: When he returned to court, he often gifted powerful figures; public opinion thereby thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he often sent gifts to the powerful, and opinion thought less of him for it.

sentences.zh: 十年卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died, age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year, at sixty.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，贈開府儀同三司、中書監、青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian, posthumously granted Grand Mentor with ceremonies equal to the Three Excellencies, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he was posthumously made grand mentor with ceremonies equal to the three excellencies, supervisor of the secretariat, and governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子閣卿，尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Geqing was a Masters of Writing lang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Geqing served as a masters of writing lang.

sentences.zh: 閣卿弟衡卿，有識學，開府參軍事。

translations.literal: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing had judgment and learning; staff member in a grand mentor's office.
translations.idiomatic: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing was learned and discerning and served as staff in a grand mentor's office.

sentences.zh: 隋大業初，卒於太常丞。

translations.literal: Early in Daye of Sui, he died as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Sui's Daye reign he died as vice director of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 元文遙，字德遠，河南洛陽人，魏昭成皇帝六世孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, a man of Luoyang in Henan; sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, was from Luoyang in Henan commandery, a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

sentences.zh: 五世祖常山王遵。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.

sentences.zh: 父晞，有孝行，父卒，廬於墓側而終。

translations.literal: His father Xi had filial conduct; when his father died, he dwelt by the tomb until he died himself.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xi was famed for filial piety; when his own father died, he lived by the tomb until he died there.

sentences.zh: 文遙貴，贈特進、開府儀同三司、中書監，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously granted Special Advancement, Grand Mentor equal to Three Excellencies, Supervisor of Secretariat, posthumous name Xiao (Filial).
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously made special advancement, grand mentor equal to the three excellencies, and supervisor of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Filial.

sentences.zh: 文遙敏慧夙成，濟陰王暉業每云：「此子王佐才也。

translations.literal: Wenyao from youth was keen and clever; Prince of Jiyin Huiye often said: "This boy is talent for assisting a king.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao was clever from childhood. The prince of Jiyin, Huiye, often said, "This child has the makings of a king's helper.

sentences.zh: 」暉業嘗大會賓客，有人將《何遜集》初入洛，諸賢皆贊賞之。

translations.literal: " Huiye once gathered guests in great assembly; someone brought the Collected Works of He Xun newly into Luoyang; all the worthies praised it.
translations.idiomatic: " Once Huiye held a great gathering of guests. Someone brought He Xun's collected works, newly arrived in Luoyang, and every worthy present praised them.

sentences.zh: 河間邢卲試命文遙：「誦之幾遍可得？

translations.literal: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many times through before you can?
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many readings before you can?

sentences.zh: 」文遙一覽便誦，時年十餘歲。

translations.literal: " Wenyao read once and recited; he was then just over ten.
translations.idiomatic: " Wenyao read it once and recited it; he was barely past ten.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王曰：「我家千里駒，今定如何？

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiyin said: "My house's thousand-li colt—what is he now?
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Jiyin said, "My house's thousand-li colt—what has he become?

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「此殆古來未有。」

translations.literal: " Xing said: "This is probably without precedent since antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "This is probably unmatched since antiquity."

sentences.zh: 起家員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His first office was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, outside the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: He began office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, outside the regular quota.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，服闋，除太尉東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: He suffered father's mourning; when mourning ended, made Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and mourning, he was made libationer in the eastern pavilion of the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 以天下方亂，遂解官侍養，隱於林慮山。

translations.literal: As the realm was in turmoil, he resigned office to tend his mother and hid on Mount Linlü.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm in turmoil, he resigned to care for his mother and lived in seclusion on Mount Linlü.

sentences.zh: 武定中，文襄徵為大將軍府功曹。

translations.literal: In Wuding, Gao Cheng summoned him as Staff Officer of the Grand General's government office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era Gao Cheng summoned him as staff officer in the grand general's office.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，於登壇所受中書舍人，宣傳文武號令。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, at the altar of enthronement he received the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer, proclaiming civil and military orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, at the enthronement altar he was made secretariat drafting officer and proclaimed civil and military orders.

sentences.zh: 楊遵彥每云：「堪解穰侯印者，必在斯人。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyian often said: "He who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyian often said, "The man who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this one.

sentences.zh: 」後忽被中旨幽執，竟不知所由。

translations.literal: " Later he was suddenly imprisoned by secret imperial order, and in the end none knew the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was suddenly seized on a secret imperial order; in the end no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 如此積年。

translations.literal: Thus for many years.
translations.idiomatic: He remained so for many years.

sentences.zh: 文宣後自幸禁獄，執手愧謝，親解所著金帶及御服賜之，卽日起為尚書祠部郎中。

translations.literal: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in ashamed apology, personally removed his gold belt and imperial robes and bestowed them, and that same day raised him to Lang in the Sacrificial Affairs section of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in apology, removed his own gold belt and court robes to give him, and that same day made him lang in the sacrificial affairs section of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 孝昭攝政，除大丞相府功曹參軍，典機密。

translations.literal: When Gao Yan acted as regent, appointed Staff Officer in the Grand Chancellor's government office, overseeing secrets.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan acted as regent, Wenyao was made staff officer in the grand chancellor's office and handled confidential matters.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，除中書侍郎，封永樂縣伯，參軍國大事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, made Secretariat Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Yongle county, and deliberated on great affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan took the throne, Wenyao was made secretariat attendant, enfeoffed as baron of Yongle county, and took part in great affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 及帝大漸，與平秦王歸彥、趙郡王叡等同受顧託，迎立武成。

translations.literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, together with Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others he received final charge and welcomed Gao Zhan to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was near death, he and Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others received the final charge and installed Gao Zhan.

sentences.zh: 卽位，任遇轉隆，歷給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: Upon enthronement his favor grew ever higher; he passed through Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Chamberlain for Attendants, Supervisor of Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Zhan took the throne, Wenyao's favor rose still higher. He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, chamberlain for attendants, and supervisor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天統二年，詔特賜姓高氏，籍屬宗正，子弟依例歲時入朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiantong, an edict specially granted the surname Gao; registration placed under the Director of Imperial Clan; sons and younger brothers per regulation attended court at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiantong an edict specially granted him the surname Gao, registered him with the director of the imperial clan, and allowed his sons and younger brothers to attend seasonal court audiences by regulation.

sentences.zh: 再遷尚書左僕射，進封寧都郡公、侍中。

translations.literal: Promoted again to Left Vice Director of Masters of Writing; advanced to Duke of Ningdu commandery, still chamberlain for attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to left vice director of the masters of writing and advanced to duke of Ningdu commandery while retaining the post of chamberlain for attendants.

sentences.zh: 文遙歷事三主，明達世務，每臨軒，多命宣勑，號令文武，聲韻高朗，發吐無滯。

translations.literal: Wenyao served three sovereigns, clear in worldly affairs; whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his civil and military orders rang high and clear, delivered without hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao served three sovereigns and knew the affairs of the age. Whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his voice rang clear, and he delivered civil and military orders without stumbling.

sentences.zh: 然探測上旨，時有委巷之言，故不為知音所重。

translations.literal: Yet probing the sovereign's intent, he sometimes had alley language, and so was not greatly valued by those who understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in reading the sovereign's mind he sometimes used coarse speech, and men of discernment did not esteem him highly.

sentences.zh: 齊因魏朝，宰縣多用廝濫，至於士流恥居百里。

translations.literal: Qi inherited Wei; county magistrates were often base appointees, until gentlemen would be ashamed to hold a hundred-li post.
translations.idiomatic: Qi followed Wei in making county magistrates too often from lowborn men, until gentlemen were ashamed to govern a hundred-li district.

sentences.zh: 文遙以縣令為字人之切，遂請革選。

translations.literal: Wenyao held that the magistrate was crucial to caring for the people, and so requested reform of selection.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao held that the magistrate was the hinge of caring for the people and asked to reform how they were chosen.

sentences.zh: 於是密令搜揚貴遊子弟，發勑用之。

translations.literal: Thereupon secret orders searched out noble scions; edicts issued to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Secret orders then sought out sons of great houses, and edicts put them in office.

sentences.zh: 猶恐其披訴，總召集神武門，令趙郡王叡宣旨唱名，厚加慰喻。

translations.literal: Still fearing their appeals and complaints, all were summoned at the Shenwu Gate; Prince of Zhao Jun Rui was ordered to proclaim names and offer words of thick consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing they would appeal, he gathered them all at Shenwu Gate and had Prince of Zhao Jun Rui read the edict, call each name, and speak words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 士人為縣，自此始也。

translations.literal: Gentlemen serving as county magistrates began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this gentlemen began to serve as county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 旣與趙彥深、和士開同被任遇，雖不如彥深清貞守道，又不為士開貪淫亂政，在於季、孟之間。

translations.literal: As he shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai, though he was not like Yanshen in purity and holding the Way, nor like Shikai in greedy debauchery and disordering government, he stood between the second and third.
translations.idiomatic: He shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai. He was not so pure and steadfast as Yanshen, nor so greedy and corrupt as Shikai, but stood between them.

sentences.zh: 然性和厚，與物無競，故時論不在彥深之下。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was genial and thick, without contention with others, and so contemporary opinion did not rank him below Yanshen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was mild and easy by nature and did not contend with others, and opinion did not place him below Yanshen.

sentences.zh: 初，文遙自洛遷鄴，惟有地十頃，家貧，所資衣食而已。

translations.literal: At first, when Wenyao moved from Luoyang to Ye, he had only ten qing of land; the family was poor—enough only for food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyao first moved from Luoyang to Ye he had only ten qing of land; the household was poor and had barely enough to eat and wear.

sentences.zh: 魏之將季，宗姓被侮，有人冒相侵奪，文遙卽以與之。

translations.literal: As Wei neared its end, clan names were insulted; someone falsely seized and encroached; Wenyao at once yielded it to him.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei neared its fall, clan members were bullied. Someone seized his land by force; Wenyao at once yielded it.

sentences.zh: 及貴，此人尚在，乃將家逃竄。

translations.literal: When he rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his household.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenyao rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his family.

sentences.zh: 文遙大驚，追加慰撫，還以與之。

translations.literal: Wenyao was greatly alarmed, pursued him with comfort, and again yielded it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao was alarmed, sent after him with reassurances, and again offered him the land.

sentences.zh: 彼人愧而不受，彼此俱讓，遂為閑田。

translations.literal: The other man was ashamed and would not accept; each yielded to the other, and it became idle land.
translations.idiomatic: The man was ashamed and would not take it; each insisted on yielding, and the field lay fallow.

sentences.zh: 至後主嗣位，趙郡王叡、婁定遠等謀出和士開，文遙亦參其議。

translations.literal: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao also joined the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao joined the plot.

sentences.zh: 叡見殺，文遙由是出為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Rui was killed; Wenyao thereby went out as Governor of Western Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was killed, and Wenyao was sent out as governor of western Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 詣士開別，士開曰：「處得言地，使元家兒作令仆，深愧朝廷。

translations.literal: Taking leave of Shikai, Shikai said: "The post you received is fair ground; to make a Yuan-family lad chancellor-in-chief deeply shames the court.
translations.idiomatic: When he took leave of Shikai, Shikai said, "You have been given a post that speaks for itself; to make a Yuan boy chancellor and vice chancellor is a deep shame to the court.

sentences.zh: 」旣言而悔，仍執手慰勉之。

translations.literal: " Having spoken, he regretted it and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.
translations.idiomatic: " Having said it, he regretted his words and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.

sentences.zh: 猶慮文遙自疑，用其子行恭為尚書郎，以慰其心。

translations.literal: Still fearing Wenyao's self-doubt, he employed his son Xinggong as Masters of Writing lang to comfort his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing Wenyao would doubt him, he appointed Wenyao's son Xinggong as a masters of writing lang to set his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 士開死，自東徐州刺史徵入朝，竟不用，卒。

translations.literal: When Shikai died, summoned from Governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, he was ultimately not employed and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Shikai died he was summoned from governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, but was never used and died.

sentences.zh: 行恭美姿貌，有父風，兼俊才，位中書舍人，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Xinggong had beautiful appearance, his father's manner, and moreover brilliant talent; he reached Secretariat Drafting Officer, awaiting edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong was handsome, had his father's bearing, and was gifted besides. He reached secretariat drafting officer and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，陽休之等十八人同入關，稍遷司勳下大夫。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together; he was gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master in the Bureau of Merits.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together with him. He rose gradually to lower grand master in the bureau of merits.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，位尚書郎，坐事徙瓜州而卒。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang of Sui he reached Masters of Writing lang; on account of offense he was banished to Guazhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui's Kaihuang reign he became a masters of writing lang; for an offense he was banished to Guazhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 行恭少頗驕恣，文遙令與范陽盧思道交遊。

translations.literal: Xinggong in youth was rather proud and self-willed; Wenyao had him associate with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong was rather proud in youth; Wenyao had him keep company with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 文遙嘗謂思道云：「小兒比日微有所知，是大弟之力，然白擲劇飲，甚得師風。

translations.literal: Wenyao once told Sidao: "The boy lately knows a little—this is elder brother's doing; yet his white-dice gambling and heavy drinking very much take the master's style.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao once told Sidao, "The boy has learned a little lately—your doing as elder brother; but his dice-playing and hard drinking are very much in your master's style.

sentences.zh: 」思道答云：「郎辭情俊邁，自是克荷堂構，而白擲劇飲，亦天性所得。

translations.literal: " Sidao answered: "Your son's rhetoric is lofty and sharp—he can surely bear the hall's beam; yet white-dice gambling and heavy drinking are also gifts of nature."
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao answered, "Your son's eloquence is sharp and lofty—he can surely uphold the family hall; but dice and deep cups are also his nature."

sentences.zh: 」行恭弟行如，亦聰慧早成，武平末，任著作佐郎。

translations.literal: " Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was also clever and precocious; late in Wuping he was appointed assistant in the Writings Office.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing Gong's younger brother Xing Ru was clever and precocious too; late in Wuping he served as an assistant in the Writings Office.

sentences.zh: 趙彥深，自云南陽宛人，漢太傅熹之後。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshen was a man of Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen came from Wan in Nanyang, a descendant of Han Grand Tutor Zhao Xi.

sentences.zh: 高祖父難，為清河太守，有惠政，遂家焉，清河後改為平原，故為平原人也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Nan was prefect of Qinghe; his kindly governance made the family settle there; Qinghe was later changed to Pingyuan, so he was reckoned a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Nan had been prefect of Qinghe; his fair rule made the family settle there. Qinghe was later renamed Pingyuan, so they counted as men of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 本名隱，避齊廟諱，改以字行。

translations.literal: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he took his courtesy name as his public name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yin; to avoid the Qi temple taboo he went by his courtesy name instead.

sentences.zh: 父奉伯，仕魏位中書舍人、行洛陽令。

translations.literal: His father Fengbo held office in Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fengbo had served Wei as secretariat gentleman and acting magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 彥深貴，贈司空。

translations.literal: When Yanshen became eminent, [Fengbo] was posthumously invested as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yanshen rose to prominence, Fengbo was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 彥深幼孤貧，事母甚孝。

translations.literal: Yanshen was orphaned young and poor, and served his mother with extreme filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen lost his father early and grew up poor, yet served his mother with fierce devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十歲，曾候司徒崔光。

translations.literal: At age ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he once called on Minister over the Masses Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 光謂賓客曰：「古人觀眸子以知人，此人當必遠至。

translations.literal: Guang said to the guests: "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know men — this one will surely go far.
translations.idiomatic: Guang told the guests, "The ancients read the whites of the eyes to know a man — this boy will go far.

sentences.zh: 」性聰敏，善書計，安閑樂道，不雜交遊，為雅論所歸服。

translations.literal: " By nature he was intelligent and quick, skilled at writing and reckoning, peaceful and devoted to the Way, not mingling in social rounds — refined opinionists looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He was bright and quick by nature, skilled at writing and reckoning, easy in manner and devoted to the Way, and kept out of casual company — men of taste deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 昧爽，輒自掃門外，不使人見，率以為常。

translations.literal: At daybreak he would sweep outside the gate himself, not letting others see — he made it his constant habit.
translations.idiomatic: Each dawn he swept outside the gate himself and would not let others watch — he made it a daily habit.

sentences.zh: 初為尚書令司馬子如賤客，供寫書。

translations.literal: At first he was a menial guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, supplying copy work.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a lowly guest of Minister over the Masses Sima Ziru, hired to copy documents.

sentences.zh: 子如善其無誤，欲將入觀省舍。

translations.literal: Ziru was pleased that he made no mistakes and wanted to bring him in to view the administration quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru was pleased that he never erred and meant to bring him inside to see the offices.

sentences.zh: 隱靴無氊，衣帽穿弊，子如給之。

translations.literal: Yin wore boots without felt lining, hat and clothes worn and tattered — Ziru supplied him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wore unlined boots and threadbare hat and clothes; Ziru furnished him.

sentences.zh: 用為書令史，月餘，補正令史。

translations.literal: He was employed as a clerical officer in the secretariat, and after a month was promoted to regular clerical officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a secretariat clerical officer and, after a month, promoted to regular clerical officer.

sentences.zh: 神武在晉陽，索二史，子如舉彥深。

translations.literal: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was at Jinyang and asked for the two histories; Ziru recommended Yanshen.

sentences.zh: 後拜子如開府參軍，超拜水部郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, and was leap-promoted to director of the water section.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Ziru's metropolitan administration staff officer, then leap-promoted to director of the water section.

sentences.zh: 及文襄為尚書令攝選，沙汰諸曹郎，彥深以地寒被出為滄州別駕，辭不行。

translations.literal: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and oversaw selection, he culled the various bureau directors — Yanshen, because of low birth, was dismissed to be Administrator in Support of Cangzhou, and he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng became Minister over the Masses and took charge of selection, he culled the bureau directors. Yanshen, judged too humble in origin, was sent out as administrator in support of Cangzhou; he declined and would not go.

sentences.zh: 子如言於神武，徵補大丞相功曹參軍，專掌機密，文翰多出其手，稱為敏給。

translations.literal: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; he was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, exclusively handling secrets; most documents came from his hand, and he was called quick and responsive.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru spoke to Gao Huan; Yanshen was summoned and made staff officer for merit affairs in the Great Chancellor's office, handling secrets alone. Most papers passed through his hand, and men called him quick and sure.

sentences.zh: 神武曾與對坐，遣造軍令，以手捫其額曰：「若天假卿年，必大有所至。

translations.literal: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered him to draft a military command; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said: "If Heaven grants you years, you will surely reach great heights.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan once sat facing him and ordered a military command drafted; he stroked Yanshen's forehead and said, "If Heaven grants you years, you will go far.

sentences.zh: 」每謂司徒孫騰曰：「彥深小心恭慎，曠古絕倫。」

translations.literal: " He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng: "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: " He often told Minister over the Masses Sun Teng, "Yanshen is careful and reverent beyond anything in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 及神武崩，秘喪事，文襄慮河南有變，仍自巡撫，乃委彥深後事，轉大行臺都官郎中。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan died they concealed the mourning; Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect on his own, entrusting the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died the mourning was kept secret. Gao Cheng feared trouble in Henan and went to inspect in person, leaving the aftermath to Yanshen and making him metropolitan administration section director.

sentences.zh: 臨發，握手泣曰：「以母弟相托，幸得此心。

translations.literal: When about to depart he clasped hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — may I have this heart.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving he clasped Yanshen's hands and wept: "I entrust my mother and younger brother to you — trust that my heart is with you.

sentences.zh: 」旣而內外寧靜，彥深之力。

translations.literal: " Thereupon inside and outside were quiet — Yanshen's doing.
translations.idiomatic: " Inside and outside thereupon grew quiet — Yanshen's doing.

sentences.zh: 及還發喪，深加褒美，乃披郡縣簿為選，封安國縣伯。

translations.literal: When [Gao Cheng] returned to announce the mourning he praised him greatly, opened the register of commanderies and counties for selections, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Anguo county.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to announce the mourning he praised Yanshen at length, opened the commandery-and-county register for selection, and enfeoffed him as marquis of Anguo county.

sentences.zh: 從征潁川，時引水灌城，城雉將沒，西魏將王思政猶欲死戰。

translations.literal: On the campaign at Yingchuan they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon be submerged, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still wanted to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yingchuan campaign they diverted water to flood the city; the battlements would soon go under, yet Western Wei general Wang Sizheng still meant to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 文襄令彥深單身入城告喻，卽日降之，便手牽思政出城。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng ordered Yanshen to enter the city alone to persuade; that same day they surrendered, and he personally led Sizheng out by the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent Yanshen into the city alone to persuade them; that same day they surrendered, and he led Sizheng out by the hand.

sentences.zh: 先是，文襄謂彥深曰：「吾昨夜夢獵，遇一群豕，吾射盡獲之，獨一大豕不可得。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Cheng had said to Yanshen: "Last night I dreamed of hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had told Yanshen, "Last night I dreamed I was hunting and met a herd of swine; I shot and took them all, but one great boar I could not get.

sentences.zh: 卿言當為吾取，須臾獲豕而進。

translations.literal: You said you would take it for me — in a moment you had the boar and came in.
translations.idiomatic: You said you would take it for me — and in a moment you had the boar and came in.

sentences.zh: 」至是，文襄笑曰：「夢驗矣。

translations.literal: " At this Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Gao Cheng laughed: "The dream is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」卽解思政佩刀與彥深曰：「使卿常獲此利。」

translations.literal: " Thereupon he removed Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying: "May you always win such profit."
translations.idiomatic: " He then took Sizheng's belt dagger and gave it to Yanshen, saying, "May you always win such profit."

sentences.zh: 彥深歷事累朝，常參機近，溫柔謹慎，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Yanshen served successive courts, constantly in close counsel, gentle and cautious, joy and anger never showing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen served successive reigns, always near the inner counsel, gentle and cautious, never letting joy or anger show on his face.

sentences.zh: 自皇建以還，禮遇稍重，每有引見，或升御榻，常呼官號而不名也。

translations.literal: From Huangjian onward his treatment grew somewhat heavier; whenever summoned he might ascend the imperial couch; he was often called by office title and not by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: From Huangjian on his honors grew weightier; when summoned he might even mount the imperial couch, and the emperor often called him by office title rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 凡諸選舉，先令銓定，提獎人物，皆行業為先，輕薄之徒，弗之齒也。

translations.literal: In all selections he would first weigh and fix the list, promoting persons by conduct first — the frivolous were never enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: In every appointment he weighed candidates first and promoted men of character; the frivolous never made his list.

sentences.zh: 孝昭旣執朝權，群臣密多勸進，彥深獨不致言。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xiaozhao took hold of court power, many ministers privately urged accession; Yanshen alone did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaozhao seized court power, many ministers privately urged him to take the throne; Yanshen alone kept silent.

sentences.zh: 孝昭嘗謂王晞云：「若言眾心皆謂天下有歸，何不見彥深有語？

translations.literal: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi: "If the crowd says everyone's heart agrees the empire has its destination, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao once said to Wang Xi, "If men say all hearts agree the realm has found its lord, why have you never heard Yanshen say so?

sentences.zh: 」晞以告，彥深不獲已，陳請，其為時重如此。

translations.literal: " Xi told him; Yanshen could not refuse further and submitted a memorial urging it — such was how the times valued him.
translations.idiomatic: " Xi told Yanshen; unable to refuse further, Yanshen submitted a memorial urging accession — such was the weight he carried in his age.

sentences.zh: 常遜言恭己，未嘗以驕矜待物，所以或出或處，去而復還。

translations.literal: He was habitually yielding and self-restraining, never treating others with arrogance — hence he might leave office and return again.
translations.idiomatic: He was habitually yielding and restrained, never arrogant toward others — so he might leave office and be called back again.

sentences.zh: 母傅氏，雅有操識。

translations.literal: His mother, née Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Fu, was refined in conduct and judgment.

sentences.zh: 彥深三歲，傅便孀居，家人欲以改適，自誓以死。

translations.literal: When Yanshen was three, Fu was already a widow; the family wished her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshen was three, Lady Fu was already a widow; the family wanted her to remarry, but she swore she would die first.

sentences.zh: 彥深五歲，傅謂之曰：「家貧兒小，何以能濟？

translations.literal: When Yanshen was five, Fu said to him: "The house is poor and you are small — how can we get by?
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshen was five, Lady Fu said to him, "We are poor and you are small — how can we live?

sentences.zh: 」彥深泣而言曰：「若天哀矜，兒大當仰報。

translations.literal: " Yanshen wept and said: "If Heaven pities us, when I grow up I shall repay you looking up.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanshen wept and said, "If Heaven takes pity, when I am grown I shall repay you on my knees.

sentences.zh: 」傅感其意，對之流涕。

translations.literal: " Fu was moved by his intent and wept facing him.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Fu was moved by his words and wept with him.

sentences.zh: 及彥深拜太常卿，還，不脫朝服，先入見母，跪陳幼小孤露，蒙訓得至於此。

translations.literal: When Yanshen was appointed grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not remove court dress but went first to see his mother, kneeling and stating that from childhood he was orphaned and exposed, yet through her instruction had come to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshen was made grand master of ceremonies and returned, he did not change out of court dress but went first to his mother, knelt, and said that as a small orphan he had come to this only through her teaching.

sentences.zh: 母子相泣久之，然後改服。

translations.literal: Mother and son wept together a long while, then only did he change clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and son wept together a long while before he changed his clothes.

sentences.zh: 後為宜陽國太妃。

translations.literal: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later she was made grand princess dowager of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 彥深有七子，仲將知名。

translations.literal: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the notable one.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen had seven sons; Zhongjiang was the one of note.

sentences.zh: 仲將，沉敏有父風，溫良恭儉，雖對妻子，亦未嘗怠慢，終日儼然。

translations.literal: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's air, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even toward wife and children he never slackened, solemn all day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjiang was deep and keen with his father's manner, warm, mild, respectful and thrifty — even with wife and children he never slackened, grave all day long.

sentences.zh: 學涉群書，善草隸。

translations.literal: He studied widely among books and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and was skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 雖與弟書，書字楷正，云草不可不解，若施之於人，卽似相輕易，若與當家中卑幼，又恐其疑所在宜爾，是以必須隸筆。

translations.literal: Though writing letters to his younger brothers, the characters were in proper regular script; he said cursive cannot be left unlearned, but to use it on people is like slighting them lightly; yet with junior kin in the household one fears they will suspect one should naturally write that way — so one must use clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Even in letters to his younger brothers he wrote in proper regular script. He said cursive must be mastered, yet to use it on others is to treat them lightly; with juniors in the household one fears they will think that is simply how one should write to them — so the brush must be clerical.

sentences.zh: 彥深乞轉以萬年縣子授之。

translations.literal: Yanshen begged transfer to grant his son the enfeoffment as viscount of Wannian county.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen asked that his own enfeoffment be transferred to make his son viscount of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 位給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He held posts as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as attendant gentleman of the yellow gate and regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，位吏部郎，終於安州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was director of the personnel section, and ended as governor of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he was director of the personnel section and ended as governor of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊朝宰相，善始令終唯彥深一人。

translations.literal: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.
translations.idiomatic: Among Northern Qi chancellors, only Yanshen began well and ended well.

sentences.zh: 然諷朝廷以子叔堅為中書侍郎，頗招物議。

translations.literal: Yet he urged the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director — this drew considerable talk.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he pressed the court to make his son Shujian secretariat vice director, which drew sharp talk.

sentences.zh: 時馮子琮子慈明、祖珽子君信並相繼居中書，故時語云：「馮、祖及趙，穢我鳳池。

translations.literal: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin in succession held posts in the secretariat, so the saying ran: "Feng, Zu, and Zhao are befouling our phoenix pool.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Feng Zicong's son Ciming and Zu Ting's son Junxin took the secretariat in turn, so people said, "Feng, Zu, and Zhao — they're fouling the phoenix pool.

sentences.zh: 」然叔堅身材最劣。

translations.literal: " Yet Shujian's physique was the worst of all.
translations.idiomatic: " Of the three, Shujian's looks were the worst.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
